title: Lemon and Sausage Risotto
description: An oven-baked sausage risotto with lemon zest and juice, finished with parsley and basil.
imageAlt: Creamy homemade lemon risotto with irregular browned sausage pieces, black pepper, herbs and lemon zest.
imageCaption: Cookbook image · lemon and sausage risotto
personalNote: This is the lemon version. Keep the juice for the end and add it a bit at a time, so we can stop when it tastes right for us.
equipment: Large oven-safe pot with an oven-safe lid
advancePrep: Air-fry the sausages until fully cooked according to their packet, then slice them thinly. Wash the lemon and zest it before juicing. Pick the basil leaves off the stalks and chop the parsley.
importantNotes: Four portions means two dinners for both of us. Garlic bread can help on the second night if we have a bit more on the first. We’re using the zest and juice of one lemon. Don’t wash the rice. Keep Parmesan at the table if we want the second dinner dairy-free, and use dairy-free sausage and stock too. For the batch, we can swap 300 g sausage for 500 g chicken or 500 g of 5% lean pork mince; check the swap note for the cooking changes. Times are estimates and don’t include air-frying the sausage.

ingredients.name: Sausages
ingredients.note: Air-fry until fully cooked, then slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.note: Zest and juice. Use only the yellow zest, avoiding the bitter white pith.

ingredients.name: Basil leaves
ingredients.note: Pick the leaves off the stalks.

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.note: Add to individual servings if wanted; leave off the dairy-free second-dinner portions.

groups.title: If we want a little extra on night two

ingredients.name: Garlic bread
ingredients.note: Optional with the second dinner if we ate a bit more on the first night. Heat following the packet.

steps.title: Prepare and preheat
steps.description: Peel and chop the garlic and onion. Air-fry the sausages until cooked, following the packet, and slice them thinly. Zest the lemon before you juice it, and keep the juice aside. Pick the basil leaves, chop the parsley, put the oven on at 180°C and boil the measured water.
steps.tip: If you are changing the protein, follow the swap note before beginning.

steps.title: Soften the onion and garlic
steps.description: Put the sausage in the oven-safe pot on medium heat. Add the garlic and onion and squish them around for 5 minutes, until the onion softens.

steps.title: Add the rice, stock and lemon zest
steps.description: Add the unwashed risotto rice, stock cubes and lemon zest, and mix them through. Keep the lemon juice for the end.
steps.tip: Keep the lemon juice aside for the end. There are no tomatoes or fennel seeds in this version.

steps.title: Add the water and bring to the boil
steps.description: Pour in the boiled water and mix. If the meat is fully cooked, taste the liquid and add salt only if it needs it. A little less salty is fine—Parmesan at the table will add some too. Bring it to the boil.
steps.warning: If you swapped in raw chicken or mince, wait until the meat is fully cooked before tasting the liquid. Adjust the seasoning after baking instead.

steps.title: Bake the covered risotto
steps.description: Once it’s boiling, cover with the oven-safe lid and put it in the oven for 30 minutes. Check the rice is cooked when it comes out, and remember the pot handles will still be hot.
steps.tip: If using a chicken or mince swap, check that the meat is fully cooked too: its centre should reach 75°C for 30 seconds. Continue cooking and recheck if needed.
steps.warning: Use oven gloves: the pot, lid and handles will stay hot after baking.

steps.title: Finish with lemon and herbs
steps.description: Mix in the black pepper, parsley and basil. Add the lemon juice a little at a time and taste as you go, until it’s as lemony as we like it.
steps.doneness: Creamy risotto with a fresh lemon flavour.
steps.tip: Adding the juice gradually lets you control the sharpness.

steps.title: Dinner tonight, and a little help for night two
steps.description: Keep Parmesan at the table so we can add it to individual plates. This makes two dinners for both of us. If we have a bit more tonight and the second dinner is smaller, we can have garlic bread with it—just heat it following the packet.
steps.tip: Add cheese to individual plates instead of the whole pot.

substitutions.title: Swap the protein
substitutions.text: For this original batch, interchange 300 g sausage with 500 g chicken or 500 g of 5% lean pork mince. The numbered ingredient quantities scale with the portion control, but these swap quantities describe the batch. Air-fry sausage until fully cooked according to its packet, then slice it. For chicken, cut into small pieces and cook it in the pot with the aromatics; it must be fully cooked by the end of baking. For pork mince, break it up in the pot and cook it through before continuing. If using raw chicken or mince, wait until the meat is fully cooked before tasting the cooking liquid.

substitutions.title: Black pepper
substitutions.text: Coarsely crushed pepper or pepper powder both work.

substitutions.title: Dairy-free second-dinner portions
substitutions.text: Leave Parmesan off those portions and use sausages and stock cubes without dairy ingredients.

troubleshooting.title: Controlling the lemon flavour
troubleshooting.text: Add the lemon juice in stages at the end and taste as you go.

troubleshooting.title: Keeping the rice creamy
troubleshooting.text: Leave the risotto rice unwashed so its starch stays in the dish.

storage: Put the second dinner into small containers so it cools quickly, ideally within 1 hour. Keep it in the fridge and eat within 24 hours. Freeze it if we’re saving it longer, and keep Parmesan separate if we want it dairy-free.
reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. Stir or turn it during microwave reheating to avoid cold pockets.
foodSafety: Cook sausage fully before slicing. For chicken or pork mince swaps, check the meat is fully cooked before tasting the liquid or serving. A thermometer check is 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Use oven gloves for the hot pot and lid.
servingSuggestion: Two dinners for both of us. Add Parmesan to individual plates if we want it. If we eat a bit more on the first night, serve the second dinner with garlic bread.
